j4.1: Normalizes a copy of the stream so that the RMS becomes 1, then scales each dimension with a learned weight. The stream itself does not change.
j4.2: Makes one query per token: what this position is looking for. 32 heads × 128.
j4.3: Builds one key per token: what the position offers. 8 KV heads × 128. Written to the KV cache.
j4.4: Builds one value per token: what gets passed on if the position is selected. Written to the KV cache.
j4.5: No weight. A fixed formula that rotates Q and K depending on position, so that attention can sense distance.
j4.6: No weight. Compares every query with all earlier keys and turns the scores into weights that sum to 1.
j4.7: No weight. Here, and only here, information moves between tokens.
j4.8: Mixes the results of the 32 heads into one contribution with the width of the stream, 4096.
j4.9: No weight. The attention contribution is added to the stream. Nothing is overwritten.
j4.10: The same thing as g₁, but before the MLP and with its own weights.
j4.11: 14,336 detectors. Each column is a pattern compared with the token vector.
j4.12: One value per detector, scaled by the gate.
j4.13: No weight. The gate lets through the detectors that fired and is multiplied element-wise with up.
j4.14: Compresses back to 4096 and writes the MLP contribution. Each row is what one detector writes to the stream.
j4.15: No weight. The MLP contribution is added. The stream moves on to the next layer.
j4.16: Total weights in one layer: {{total}} parameters. Times 32 layers that is about 6.98 billion; the rest of the 8.03 billion is the embedding and the LM head.
j4.18: This is the row for the token “den” as it enters the layer, after all previous layers. It carries everything known about the position so far.
j4.20: RMSNorm divides every number by the RMS of the vector, so the copy gets RMS 1 but keeps the same direction. The stream x itself is untouched. (The learned weight g₁ is set to 1 here.)
j4.22: Attention reads the copy for this position and for all earlier positions, and fetches what is relevant. Out comes a contribution with the same shape as x. It is small compared with x.
j4.25: The contribution is laid on top. Nothing is deleted: each dimension has only been adjusted a little. The first row is done.
j4.26: The second row starts the same way, but x now contains what attention just fetched. The copy is normalized with its own weight, g₂.
j4.28: The MLP sees only the copy for this position, no other tokens. It reshuffles the dimensions and returns a contribution with the same shape.
j4.30: The contribution is added and x moves on to the next layer, where the same two rows run again with new weights. After 32 layers, x is the sum of the embedding and 64 such contributions.
j4.31: Attention for “{{token}}”: fetches a weighted mixture of the rows above and its own (the percentages). Rows below are masked. Information moves between tokens, along T.
j4.32: MLP for “{{token}}”: only its own row is read. The dimensions are reshuffled within the row, along d. Every row goes through the same MLP weights, independent of the others.
j4.37: Neurons that fire write their direction into the stream, which makes some continuations more likely: {{list}}.
j4.38: No neuron fires clearly. The MLP contribution is almost zero, and the stream passes through more or less unchanged.
j4.39: The stream is still almost only the embedding for “var”. The top guesses echo the token itself.
j4.40: The grammar has taken shape: after “den var” an intensifier or an adjective usually comes.
j4.41: Attention has fetched “Katten” and “mattan”. States that suit a cat are starting to show up.
j4.42: Later layers have drawn conclusions from the context. “trött” leads clearly.
j4.43: After the last layer: the distribution that sampling actually draws from.
j4.45: RoPE: rotate Q and K by position
j4.46: P · V: weighted sum of the values
j4.54: No weight, nothing is stored in the model file.
j4.60: New copy, now of the updated x
